text:
mei: quick design proposal for prefix eviction correctness — want sanity-checks before i turn this into an RFC
mei: problem: hot tenants spike and displace others; we also need stronger read-after-write correctness during handoffs
mei: proposal (high-level): tenant-aware spillover slab + two‑phase takeover for demotes
mei: - keep lease model for ownership (no change)
mei: - when memory pressure, instead of hard-evict, mark prefixes SOFT_SPILL and move payloads to a per-shard overflow slab (lower priority)
mei: - overflow slab is read-through but has slower access; it preserves KV residency so sequencer can still read with strong R/W ordering
mei: - demote -> an async two-phase takeover: new owner obtains takeover token (atomic CAS against lease epoch), then swaps residency pointer, then publishes tombstone/epoch update
james: interesting. how do we avoid double-apply or lost updates during the short window between token CAS and pointer swap?
mei: two guards: 1) sequencer enforces epoch check on writes, 2) takeover token includes last-applied-index; takeover aborts if remote shows newer index
omar: does this mean we need to extend the lease proto? more RPCs = more latency on handoff
sophia: +1 to correctness but worried about tail latency: overflow reads could blow p99 for affected tenants
mei: overflow slab is opt-in per-tenant and only used after a grace threshold; also we can serve overflow reads from a degraded path with circuit-breaker to fallback to a cheaper model/variant
james: can we keep metrics to route tenant-critical requests to non-spill nodes? we already tag tokens per-tenant
omar: tradeoffs on memory fragmentation too — overflow slab has to be compaction-friendly
mei: thinking of a small state machine added to prefix metadata. pseudo:
mei: ```
mei: RESIDENT -> SOFT_SPILLED -> TAKING_OVER -> EVICTED
mei: actions:
mei:  - on SOFT_SPILLED: write-through to overflow, mark tombstone=off
mei:  - TAKEOVER: CAS lease_epoch, swap residency pointer, publish epoch bump
mei: ```
sophia: nice. what about read-after-write: if a writer A writes then we handoff, readers must see A's write even if data is in overflow
mei: seq enforces order. write handler writes to primary seq log, then cache. takeover checks last-applied-index. we only swap if takeover token epoch >= last_applied of source
omar: cost question: will overflow slab cause more bytes on GPU memory due to copy-on-spill? we should prefer KV pointer indirection rather than duplicating tensors
mei: agreed—overflow should be pointer-backed where possible. we only materialize tensors on-demand and keep lightweight descriptors otherwise
james: operationally: how do we surface this in console? need metrics: spill count, takeover failures, overflow p99
mei: plan to add per-tenant counters + a global spill histogram and a takeover failure reason tag
sophia: test plan: unit tests for epoch CAS, canary with single shard, long-run perf test with synthetic hot tenants, and a correctness sim that injects race windows
infra-bot: perf-canary results available: canary/evict-spill-20260310: median read cost +8%, p99 +38% under synthetic spike
mei: good find infra-bot, thanks
omar: fallback: if takeover fails repeatedly, fallback to remote-fetch-from-primary-node with backoff (slower but safe)
james: we should add a debugging endpoint: `/prefix/debug?prefix=...` that returns lease_epoch, residency_state, last_applied_index
mei: i'll sketch the RFC with those APIs and the sim harness. aiming to ship prototype behind feature flag
sophia: sg, prioritize the correctness tests. i can pair on the sim
mei: thx everyone. i'll post the RFC draft later today and ping @here for review :thumbsup:
